correctness.rationale: For each nonpivot index k, the Jacobi rotation acts orthogonally on the pair (a_pk,a_qk), so each new component is at most the Euclidean norm of two entries whose magnitudes are at most the pre-step second-largest value s. This gives m_plus<=sqrt(2)s. The three-dimensional family B_tau has a unique pivot 1 and two entries of magnitude tau; its equal pivot diagonals force a 45-degree rotation that combines those entries into sqrt(2)tau exactly. Its spectrum is explicit, and adding cI with c=(1-kappa*beta_minus)/(kappa-1) gives an SPD matrix of condition number exactly kappa without changing the rotation. The transformed matrix has a single off-diagonal pair, so the next Jacobi step diagonalizes it. Dimension two is exact in one rotation.

originality.rationale: The maximum-element pivot rule, the orthogonal pair update, aggregate off-diagonal energy descent, and global Jacobi convergence are classical and treated as prior work. The inspected literature does not state the sharp largest-entry gap threshold, the equality law, or the arbitrary-condition-number three-dimensional spike followed by exact next-step termination. Searches across aliases and nearby published records found no implication-equivalent theorem. The main residual risk is older Jacobi literature using a max-norm or elementwise convergence formulation not exposed by the inspected sources.
residual_risks: Older Jacobi convergence literature is extensive, and the same elementary max-entry inequality may have appeared under max-norm or elementwise terminology.
The body of the 2007 Hari paper and the complete body of the 2009 Matejaš paper were not available through the inspected publisher route.
The theorem is one-step and elementwise; it does not classify max-entry behavior across an arbitrary full sweep.

value.rationale: The largest-element pivot rule is a classical Jacobi strategy, and the largest remaining off-diagonal entry is both the quantity searched to select the next pivot and a natural stopping diagnostic. The theorem identifies exactly when this diagnostic is guaranteed to improve, shows that aggregate off-diagonal descent does not protect it above the sharp gap threshold, and proves that condition number cannot rule out the transient. The equality family then resolves the behavior completely in the minimal dimension by showing exact diagonalization on the next step.
